firmographics.narrative_md:
Global Federal Credit Union (formerly Alaska USA FCU until April 2023) is a $12.066B federal credit union headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska, serving approximately 795,000 members across five states and three military installations in Italy. As one of the top 20 US credit unions by membership, GCU occupies the Large tier ($10B–$50B) within the SV2 Credit Union sub-vertical at 95% confidence. The institution is in an active digital transformation cycle — cloud-first since 2019, AI operations saving 62,000 hours annually, and a MuleSoft integration platform processing 300 million transactions per year. However, the absence of a CDO, CTO, or CIO at the executive level, combined with very low member satisfaction scores (Yelp 1.7/5), creates a paradox: significant back-office digital investment that is not yet translating into member-facing value.

Global Federal Credit Union was established in 1948 as Elmendorf Air Force Base Federal Credit Union, serving military personnel in Alaska [E-003]. The institution has grown through multiple mergers to become one of the nation's largest credit unions, rebranding from Alaska USA Federal Credit Union to Global Federal Credit Union in April 2023 [E-001]. As a federally chartered credit union regulated by NCUA, GCU is member-owned with operations spanning five US states (Alaska, Arizona, California, Washington, Idaho) and three military installations in Italy [E-001, E-042].

GFCU was benchmarked against 5 peers selected for sub-vertical match (credit union), size tier proximity, and geographic relevance: BECU ($29.5B), Mountain America FCU ($21.2B), America First CU ($22.6B), Idaho Central CU ($12.1B), and Desert Financial CU ($9.4B). Peer median overall: 3.18.

GFCU's security scores match or exceed all peers, providing a foundation for confident digital service expansion.

narrative.scqa_md:
Global Federal Credit Union is a $12.1B in assets credit union regulated by NCUA, operating since 1948 with 2,000 employees. A trajectory the analyst classifies as accelerating gives it the balance sheet to fund transformation [E-009, E-005]. Zennify's assessment places overall digital maturity at 2.2/5. The deepest capability gap is Green Products Strategy at 1.1/5 against a 2.5 peer median [E-014, E-015]. Next is Proactive Outreach & Alerts at 1.5/5 against a 2.5 peer median [E-016].

Third is Adapted Communication at 1.9/5 against a 3.5 peer median [E-001, E-002]. The issue register adds Capability gap: Employee Ideation (high severity) [E-008]. The issue register adds Capability gap: Idea Prioritization (high severity) [E-012]. Counter-signal: Secure Code Development already runs at 3.1/5 against a 2.5 peer median — a strength to build on, not rebuild. The roster shows no CISO — a named ownership gap for the capabilities below.

The question for Global Federal Credit Union is whether to close Green Products Strategy first — the constraint the other investments inherit — or continue layering point solutions on top of it and accept the compounding operating cost. Global Federal Credit Union should lead with nCino (79/100 fit) against Idea Prioritization, then sequence Tableau behind it. Closing Green Products Strategy to the peer median alone is worth 1.4 maturity points, and the capabilities that depend on it compound the gain. The analyst's own priority framing: "Enterprise-Grade Security: SVP Vanzant (ex-FBI), F5 8-product suite, Palo Alto SIEM/SOAR, CISSP-certified Director. — Security maturity de-risks data platform investment proposals.".
